title: nba 2k16
text: Really disappointed in the MyCareer mode, which is the only mode I played in this and 2k15.  It is a huge regression from last year for a number of reasons due to the way the story was put in place.  The biggest issues: 1)  In your rookie NBA season, you only play 8 games.  After those 8 games, you move on to your sophomore season where you can then play a full 82 game season.  At this point, the game has sent players all over the place in free agency, so the teams are totally different than what they will be this season.  So for instance, I cannot play more than 8 games without Tim Duncan retiring. 2)  The story is really stupid and feels forced upon you.  "The team isn't sure about signing you because you are friends with Vic."  Are you kidding?  And no matter how well you play, you get this way over-dramatic storyline that detracts from simply being a rookie trying to make it in the NBA. 3)  There just simply isn't enough content in this game that responds to how you play in your games.  There were plenty of cut scenes in 2k15 that would cater to your performance.  For instance, the coach would call you in and congratulate you for your rebounding effort or how you distribute the ball to your teammates.  In this game I haven't seen any of that (though maybe I just haven't played long enough to see it).  All of the cut scenes in 2k16 play out just like a movie (a downright terrible one).  I play games for an immersive, interactive experience where my play affects the outcome.  This game is not that at all.

text: This game COULD be great. It could be something that we all love. But a sorry excuse for steering wheel and gamepad support are my biggest issues. The game with all assists OFF still takes away a larger percentage of your steering the faster you go. 20 MPH=full steering. 45mph steering is cut by over 50%. It almost makes the game unplayable. I say this because if you get tapped by another driver and start to spin there is no way to counter steer. I have tried everything in the settings and I still get the same results no matter what they are. I could see this game getting a lot of my time but as of right now I cannot stand to have a game force vehicle physics and surface traction differences on me (dirt, tarmac, grass, ect) without a proper way to actually control the car. As it is right now I find the game playable but only on the keyboard. It seems to be the only control that does not suffer from the limited steering. As of right now I cannot recommend this game as it is. Could be great but isn't. Simple.
